operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Executive Order 11408, signed 1968-04-25 (33 FR 6459, printed 1968-04-27), revokes in section 1 Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873 (dual Federal-State office holding) and Executive Order No. 9367 of August 4, 1943 (prohibiting Government employees from instructing persons for certain Government examinations), and in section 2 all prior Executive orders insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9, naming a list of numbers. Both commands are one-time revocations performed when the order takes effect. The order has no effective-date wording, so it took effect on signing, 1968-04-25 (the printing date 1968-04-27 is an alternative reading, not an end; the day number in the held signature line is garbled, and the date rests on the census register, the Office of the Federal Register catalog and the filing line of April 25, 1968). The clause is exhausted by performance on that date (owner ruling 2026-10-28: a used one-time command is recorded as exhausted by performance, separate from any surviving consequence; the surviving consequence here is the revoked status of the named orders, which is not a command of this order). The cited source is the order's own held text, which contains the words are hereby revoked in both sections. No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11408 (33 FR 6459, Federal Register of April 27, 1968; the govinfo PDF text layer), headed Executive Order 11408, Revoking Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873, and amendatory orders, relating to dual Federal-State office holding, and Executive Order No. 9367 of August 4, 1943, signed by Lyndon B. Johnson; the census register and the Office of the Federal Register catalog give the signing date 1968-04-25, and the held text shows filing on April 25, 1968 (the day number in the signature line is garbled in the text layer). Inventory: section 1 revokes Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873 and Executive Order No. 9367 of August 4, 1943; section 2 revokes all prior Executive orders insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9, naming a list of numbers that begins with 9-2 of January 28, 1873 and ends with 10645 of November 22, 1955. The dossier's single whole-order clause covers both sections and matches. Lifecycle: both commands are one-time revocations performed when the order took effect. The order has no effective-date wording, so it took effect on signing, 1968-04-25; the printing date 1968-04-27 is an alternative reading, not an end. The clause is exhausted by performance on 1968-04-25. Dossier missing item (target provision not located, EO 11222): EO 11222 is not a target of this order; it is a cross-reference in the Office of the Federal Register editorial note on this order, which says see EO 11222 with the date May 8, 1968 although EO 11222 was signed on 1965-05-08; an order signed in 1965 cannot be a later event of this 1968 order, and nothing in this order's text names it. It is not relied on. Searches: the U.S. Code, eCFR and Office of the Federal Register disposition-note searches record no later instrument that amends, revokes or supersedes this order (the catalog's two hits are editorial cross-references, one to EO 11222 and one to 5 U.S.C. 7301 and section 735.203 of the Civil Service regulations, as described); a held-corpus search by number returns only this order's own printings; the order is not in the table of EO 12553.

W H E R E A S section 204 of the Agricultural Act of 1956 (7 U.S.C. 
1854) (hereinafter referred to as “the Act”) authorizes the President, 
whenever he determines such action appropriate, to negotiate with 
representatives of foreign governments in an effort to obtain agree­
ments lim iting the export from such countries and the importation 
into the United States of any agricultural commodity or product 
manufactured therefrom, and to issue regulations governing the entry 
or Withdrawal from warehouse of any such commodity or product to

ment of Honduras by whim  the Government of Honduras agreed that 
during the calendar year 1969 exports from such country and imports 
into the U nited States for consumption of fresh, chilled, or frozen 
cattle meat (item 106.10 of the Tariff Schedules of the United States) 
and fresh, chilled, or frozen meat of goats and sheep, except lambs 
(item 106.20 of the Tariff Schedules of the United State's) would be 
limited to an aggregate quantity of 14.1 million pounds; and
W H E R E A S an aggregate quantity in excess of 14.1 million pounds

into the United States for consumption during the calendar year 1969:

President of the United States, and pursuant to section 204. of the 
Act, it is hereby ordered that the following regulation governing the

carried o u t:

meat of goats and sheep (except lam bs)) of p art 2B, schedule 1, of 
the Tariff Schedules of the United States, the product of Honduras, 
may be entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption in 
the United States during^ the remainder of the calendar year 1969.

to the date of this order.

THE PRESIDENT 17703
Executive Order 1 1 5 6 8
EXEMPTING A. EVERETTE MadNTYRE FROM COMPULSORY  
RETIREMENT FOR AGE
W HEREAS A. Everette MacIntyre, a member of the Federal 
Trade Commission, will, during the month of February 1971, become 
subject to compulsory retirement for age under the provisions of 
section 8335 of title 5, United States Code, unless exempted therefrom 
by Executive order; and
W HEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest requires that 
Mr. MacIntyre be exempted from such compulsory retirement:
NOW, TH EREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me 
by subsection (c) of section 8335 of title 5, United States Code, I  here­
by exempt A. Everette MacIntyre from compulsory retirement for 
age until February 29,1972.
T h e W h ite H ouse,
November 16,1970.
